arxiv-2111-15235.title: Reconstructing AGN X-ray spectral parameter distributions with Bayesian methods. II. Population inference
arxiv-2111-15235.creator: Lingsong Ge, Stéphane Paltani, Dominique Eckert, Mara Salvato
arxiv-2111-15235.description: Abstract We present a new Bayesian method for reconstructing the parent distributions of X-ray spectral parameters of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in large surveys. The method uses the probability distribution function (PDF) of posteriors obtained by fitting a consistent physical model to each object with a Bayesian method.

arxiv-2411-14228.title: FocusLLaVA : A Coarse-to-Fine Approach for Efficient and Effective Visual Token Compression
arxiv-2411-14228.creator: Yuke Zhu, Chi Xie, Shuang Liang, Bo Zheng, Sheng Guo
arxiv-2411-14228.description: Abstract Recent advances on Multi-modal Large Language Models have demonstrated that high-resolution image input is crucial for model capabilities, especially for fine-grained tasks. However, high-resolution images lead to a quadratic increase in the number of visual tokens input into LLMs, resulting in significant computational costs.

pmc-10660506.title: A Fuzzy Clustering Approach to Identify Pedestrians’ Traffic Behavior Patterns
pmc-10660506.creator: Parisa Saeipour, Parvin Sarbakhsh, Saman Salemi, Fatemeh Bakhtari Aghdam
pmc-10660506.description: Background: Pattern recognition of pedestrians’ traffic behavior can enhance the management efficiency of interested groups by targeting access to them and facilitating planning via more specific surveys. This study aimed to evaluate the pedestrians’ traffic behavior pattern by fuzzy clustering algorithm and assess the factors related to higher-risk traffic behavior of pedestrians.

pmc-11500702.title: Foot darkening with age in Spheniscus penguins: applications and functions
pmc-11500702.creator: Ginger A. Rebstock, K. Pearl Wellington, P. Dee Boersma
pmc-11500702.description: The proportions of individuals in various age classes in a population of wild animals affect population trends, behaviors, learning, and social structures. Knowledge of age structure is needed for effective conservation and management of populations. However, it is not always possible to determine the age or age class of individual animals, and hence the age structure of the population.

pmc-11538411.title: Comparison of the asymmetries in foot posture, gait and plantar pressure between patients with unilateral and bilateral knee osteoarthritis based on a cross-sectional study
pmc-11538411.creator: Yi Wang, Peiming Zhang, Guocai Chen, Tao Jiang, Yonggen Zou
pmc-11538411.description: This study aimed to observe the characteristics of foot posture asymmetry and abnormal gait in patients with unilateral and bilateral knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and to explore the association between foot posture asymmetry, abnormal gait and the clinical symptoms and severity of KOA.

pmc-11603517.title: Equal rates of bone healing and reduced surgical time with iliac crest allograft compared to autograft in medial opening wedge high tibial osteotomy: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
pmc-11603517.creator: RE De Paula, A Cordeiro, AP Mozella, RD Sobral, HAAB Cobra, RSP Albuquerque
pmc-11603517.description: ObjectivesIliac crest autograft is frequently used to fill in bone defects after osteotomies. Nonetheless, surgery for bone autograft procurement is associated with morbidity and pain at the donor site. Alternatives to it have been explored, but there is no consensus to guide their application as a routine practice in several orthopedic procedures.

pmc-12436138.title: Case Report: Steroids for diabetic myonecrosis in ESKD: an unconventional treatment with unexpected success
pmc-12436138.creator: Justin David Tse, Sristhi Laller, Sourabh Kharait
pmc-12436138.description: IntroductionMyonecrosis is a rare but serious complication of diabetes, particularly in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), characterized by ischemic necrosis of the skeletal muscles. Its diagnosis is often delayed due to overlapping presentations with cellulitis or deep vein thrombosis. Treatment is traditionally limited to supportive measures such as rest and pain control, which remains the cornerstone.

pmc-12570661.title: Ex-vivo limb perfusion in military and civilian medicine: inspired by ex-vivo organ perfusion, pioneered for traumatic limb amputation and peripheral nerve regeneration
pmc-12570661.creator: Kirsten Haastert-Talini, Katherina Katsirntaki, Svenja Kankowski, Alexander Kaltenborn, Falk von Lübken, Christine Falk, Christopher Werlein, Danny Jonigk, Arjang Ruhparwar, Bettina Wiegmann
pmc-12570661.description: BackgroundTraumatic amputations have increased worldwide over the past two decades and are expected to increase by 72% by 2050. Surgical replantation provides superior functional recovery and patient satisfaction but is limited to specialized centers and restricted by short ischemia times, due to life-over-limb prioritization in patient care.

pmc-12615764.title: Double-chirped mirrors expand the bandwidth of infrared frequency combs
pmc-12615764.creator: Jacob B Khurgin
pmc-12615764.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A novel dispersion-compensation scheme based on double-chirped Bragg mirrors is implemented in a mid-infrared quantum cascade laser. As a result, stable and broadband frequency combs are generated, which are indispensable for high-precision applications in spectroscopy and metrology.Subject terms: Semiconductor lasers, Infrared spectroscopy Optical frequency combs (FCs)1 are coherent sources of electromagnetic radiation characterized by a spectrum of equally spaced, narrow spectral lines and a periodic temporal waveform.

pmc-13541901.title: Assessment of the learning curve of robotic liver resection using complexity-adjusted CUSUM analysis
pmc-13541901.creator: Jiwon Han, Hyokee Kim, Wan Joon Kim
pmc-13541901.description: Robotic liver resection (RLR) has progressively been integrated into minimally invasive hepatobiliary surgery. However, comparative evidence evaluating the learning curves of RLR and laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) while accounting for surgical complexity remains limited. This study analyzed the learning curve of RLR through complexity-adjusted cumulative sum (CA-CUSUM) analysis based on operative time and the IWATE difficulty score.

pmc-13577298.title: Occupational trauma and probable PTSD among sworn and civilian police employees
pmc-13577298.creator: Bjørn Lau, Brita Bjørkelo, Knut Inge Fostervold
pmc-13577298.description: Background: Police personnel are frequently exposed to potentially traumatic events (PTEs), increasing their risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). While much research has focused on sworn police officers (SPOs), less is known about civilian employees (Civilians) who work alongside them. This study examined trauma exposure and probable PTSD in both groups within the Norwegian Police Service (NPS).
